item.title: A thousand fewer paths to root (20 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's autonomous security pipeline reproduced 1,724 Linux kernel vulnerabilities and generated exploits for 948 distinct local privilege escalation flaws at an API cost of $1.2 million. Agents handled discovery, runtime validation, exploit development, and candidate patches before human review and maintainer reporting. The research highlights why validation must check how an exploit succeeds, after some agents gained root through a different vulnerability than the one assigned.

item.title: How We Made clarity.js 4.5% Smaller Without Sacrificing Compatibility (5 minute read)
item.description: Microsoft reduced clarity.js by 1,257 gzip bytes through more than 50 automated change, build, measure, and test experiments. Named imports and minifier settings delivered savings, while extracting small helpers sometimes increased compressed size. A larger saving from modern JavaScript output could not ship because native async functions would break Angular sites that depend on Zone.js.

item.title: You'll need nerves of steel to work with AI agents (10 minute read)
item.description: Fast, cheap coding agents can create substantial review work by deleting unrelated code, missing requirements, and making tests pass without exercising the intended behavior. More than 100 hours with Cursor's Composer 2.5 exposed failures ranging from unsolicited edits to disabled schema validation and tests that bypassed API routes. Explicit rules and reference implementations did not reliably prevent repeated mistakes.

item.title: Agentic Technical Debt and Where Orchestration Belongs in AI Agent Architecture (9 minute read)
item.description: Agent systems accumulate debt when prompts and agent loops take responsibility for approvals, side-effect retries, and audit trails. A supplier invoice dispute illustrates how to divide ownership among the model, harness, durable execution, and an orchestration control plane. A single agent inside one application may need only its harness, while processes crossing systems need explicit ownership of recovery and approval.

item.title: Nobody here writes code by hand anymore (12 minute read)
item.description: An account of adopting coding agents at Intento traces the shift from small experiments to a team that delegates code generation and reviews the output. The key change was making documentation, architectural decisions, tasks, and production logs accessible to models. Earlier failures on an established codebase were attributed to missing context that lived in people's heads, rather than the age of the code itself.

item.title: Scale Postgres Past the Slowdown – and Get $1,000 in Credits (Sponsor)
item.description: Growing Postgres databases eventually hit a wall: queries slow, dashboards lag, and adding another database starts to feel inevitable. Tiger Data keeps Postgres fast as your data grows with time-series primitives, columnar storage, and automatic partitioning. No pipelines or second system needed. Get $1,000 in credits when you sign up for free.

item.title: Graphify (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Graphify turns code and supporting material into a queryable knowledge graph with paths between concepts and an interactive browser view. Code parsing uses local tree-sitter analysis without an LLM or vector store, while document and media interpretation can use a model. Edges distinguish explicit source relationships from inferred connections, making the graph's evidence easier to inspect.

item.title: faster-chrome-devtools-skill (GitHub Repo)
item.description: This agent skill and dependency-free Node CLI control Chrome directly through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. It supports accessibility snapshots, tab management, screenshots, and raw protocol calls without requiring a separate browser MCP server. Screenshots are written to files so agents can choose when to load them into context.

item.title: A new Go API for JSON (9 minute read)
item.description: Go 1.27 makes encoding/json/v2 and encoding/json/jsontext generally available, addressing behavior and performance constraints that could not be fixed within the old API. The new defaults reject invalid UTF-8 and duplicate object names, while the packages separate Go value conversion from lower-level JSON syntax processing.

item.title: DOOM's DNA (Website)
item.description: This interactive study compares the original DOOM source with 43 descendants to explore what survives copying, porting, and translation. Structural fingerprints and call relationships can reveal ancestry even when names or source text change. In a blind test, a Go translation's functions were assigned to the correct game subsystem 60% of the time, compared with 20% for shuffled labels.

item.title: The PHP2Shell Vulnerability Heralds Cybersecurity Hell (4 minute read)
item.description: AI-assisted researchers turned a PHP crash bug reported in 2024 into a critical vulnerability capable of running arbitrary code on a server. Finding the exploit took two weeks, while four engineers spent two months developing a patch, illustrating the growing gap between discovering flaws and safely fixing them. Better funding for open-source maintainers, defensive AI tools, and formal verification could help close that gap.

item.title: Introducing Images 2.6 (3 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI's Images 2.6 brings 50% faster image generation, GIF creation, and better consistency across edits.

item.description: Ricursive released Ripple-65B Preview, a dense open-weight model with up to 1M tokens of context that reports an 80.52 score on TerminalBench 2.1 and a total development and training cost of $32 million.

item.description: Parcel 3 rewrites the bundler in Rust and reports cold builds up to 100 times faster than v2.

item.description: Anthropic's public-beta message threads let active agents send only new messages each turn, reducing median time to first token by about 35% for requests with 500k to 1M tokens while leaving token usage unchanged.

item.title: Jailbreaking my car's navigation system just so I can change the time (10 minute read)
item.description: A Renault's clock settings were inaccessible without a legitimate navigation SD card, turning a daylight-saving adjustment into a firmware reverse-engineering project. QEMU emulation exposed how a script parser's file writes and Linux's core-dump handling could combine into code execution. The eventual fix changed the stored GPS time offset from 180 minutes to 120.

item.title: The hidden latency inside your database (7 minute read)
item.description: Network-attached storage adds latency inside a database cluster, even when the application and database are close together. Local NVMe avoids that hop, but requires deliberate replication and failover to preserve durability. Workloads that fit mostly in RAM may see little benefit, while frequent cache misses and IOPS limits make storage placement worth examining.

item.title: Scaling Git at OpenAI (22 minute read)
item.description: OpenAI built Pando, a Git-compatible backend that handles pushes to unrelated branches independently and reuses cached packfiles across fetches. It reduced median push latency by nearly 80% and now serves nearly a petabyte of Git data per day. The tradeoff is weaker consistency across branches and some redundant downloads, allowing writes to scale horizontally and reads to saturate clients' network connections.

item.title: Resisting Cognitive Surrender (12 minute read)
item.description: Uncritically accepting agent output can increase technical debt while eroding the understanding needed to debug and maintain a system. Choose how much to delegate based on risk, stay involved in consequential decisions, and ask for small, comprehensible changes. When delegating more fully, use independent observability, deterministic checks, and shadow traffic to verify behavior rather than relying solely on the agent's account.

item.title: Auditioning Engineering: Software Engineering Interviews in the Age of AI (6 minute read)
item.description: Warner Music Group encourages candidates to use AI while solving realistic API integration problems against a live, randomized test server. Its system-design interview asks candidates to modify an existing system and infer causes from observed behavior. The approach emphasizes technical judgment, although building new coding exercises and training senior system-design interviewers remain costly.

item.title: The weight-space programming post is misleading (5 minute read)
item.description: This critique separates experiments that inspect small networks' raw weights from larger-model experiments that use Python and execution feedback. The Qwen result involved 50 batches of practice problems, so it does not demonstrate improvement from inspecting raw weights alone. The distinction matters when judging whether the work shows one general capability or several different engineering techniques.

item.title: djs (GitHub Repo)
item.description: djs is a JavaScript and TypeScript engine written in Rust for agent-generated scripts running in a WebAssembly sandbox. It keeps the entire VM state in one byte array, allowing execution to pause between instructions, snapshot while waiting for tools, and resume elsewhere. The focused runtime deliberately omits features such as ES modules, Intl, and a JIT.

item.title: Office Engine (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Office Engine embeds DOCX, XLSX, and PPTX viewing and editing in a browser through React or a web component. Progressive loading, Web Worker parsing, and virtualized views handle large files, while saves regenerate edited parts and preserve the original bytes elsewhere.

item.title: Three-Live (GitHub Repo)
item.description: Three-Live compiles a declarative subset of Three.js into GLB and USDZ assets for web, Android, and Apple rendering pipelines. It runs generated scripts with execution timeouts and geometry quotas, then hands the assets to platform-specific viewers. The Apache-licensed project is in Developer Preview and is not an officially supported Google product.

item.title: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming (20 minute read)
item.description: Experiments show GPT-6 Astra reading and directly editing neural network weights without gradient descent, including writing small game-playing networks from scratch. Editing 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights reduced reasoning loops and raised MATH-500 accuracy from 7.9% to 48.1% with 50 forward passes for feedback. The gains removed an obstacle to existing ability, while similar edits failed to meaningfully improve a Gemma model that rarely looped.

item.title: Could a modern chess engine on a Pentium have defeated Kasparov in 1996? (15 minute read)
item.description: A port of Stockfish running on a 200 MHz Pentium Pro with 64 MB of RAM reaches a measured rating of 3180 at 30 seconds per move. The experiment attributes much of chess engines' progress to better search and evaluation rather than faster hardware. Its roughly 3300 rating at classical time controls is extrapolated from shorter games, and readers can play the machine online.

item.title: How we halved DNS build delay and cut memory use by 85% (18 minute read)

The changes cut peak memory by 85% and halved the delay from a DNS change to its data being written to Quicksilver without rebuilding tens of millions of records for a settings change.

At Vercel, it removed nearly 2 MB of compressed JavaScript across v0 and vercel.com, so Turbopack users can get similar savings with little manual work.

item.title: Time to rethink software security because of AI? (10 minute read)

AI now makes vulnerabilities faster to find and easier to exploit, even for nontechnical attackers. Teams will likely need automated patching, constant security monitoring, and AI-driven defense, and security will cost more.

item.description: AI agents could make technical website migrations nearly free by using the existing site as a baseline for differential tests of pages and publishing workflows. item.description: LangChain's internal agents share five components: Slack interfaces, scoped credentials, shared and personal memory, sandboxed execution, and scheduled runs. Memory remains the least solved piece.

item.title: Python and Postgres Don't Agree on What “CET” Means (9 minute read)
item.description: A timezone accepted by Python broke Mergify's merge-freeze queries because Postgres rejected it, and the investigation uncovered four names that silently differ by an hour in summer. item.title: Design Systems Should Be Fast by Default (18 minute read)

The investigation traces slow paths to repeated slot scans, layout thrashing, and animations, then supplies Playwright performance budgets that teams can run on each pull request.

item.title: Websites Should Be Printable (4 minute read)
